chapters.1.lds: Why does lost grain affect both farmers and priests?
chapters.1.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Joel. He asks the old men whether anything like this has happened before. Swarm after swarm of locusts has eaten everything. Vines are ruined, and fig trees are stripped bare. Grain and wine offerings have stopped in the LORD’s house. Farmers despair, and the joy of the people dries up. Joel tells the priests to call a fast and gather everyone. Even the wild animals cry to God as the streams dry up.
chapters.2.lds: The 2026 lesson studies inward devotion and the Spirit’s guidance. It connects Joel’s promise with Acts and Joseph Smith’s account as later applications. Who must join the gathering, and who receives the promised Spirit?
chapters.2.summary: A trumpet sounds in Zion, for the day of the LORD is near. An army advances like fire, and nothing escapes it. Yet even now God calls the people to return with all their heart. They should tear their hearts and not their clothes. He is gracious, merciful, and slow to anger. Everyone must gather, from elders to nursing infants. Then God will restore the years the locusts ate. Afterward he will pour out his Spirit on all people.
chapters.3.lds: How do the charges about sold children explain the judgment?
chapters.3.summary: In those days God will gather all nations for judgment. They scattered his people and divided his land. They cast lots for his people. They traded a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine. Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia sold Judah’s children far away. God will return their deeds on their own heads. Crowds gather in the valley of decision. The LORD will shelter his people, and Judah will be lived in forever.
